transcription.notes: Counts: read/R*.raw.txt holds one output per cipher token (dec.py), and the per-letter counts equal those of parse.py on DECODE's DOC_R*.txt files (git-ignored img/, 3504 tokens, 252 distinct in all). DECODE's transcription slips pass into the machine reading as {..} or nonsense syllables; no corrections against the images were made.

system.summary: Point-separated syllabic nomenclator: numbers 9-30 single letters, 31-60 consonant-vowel syllables in rows of five, struck numbers a second syllable table, letter pairs as syllables with the consonant disguised, about twenty three-letter code words, struck nulls.

diacritics.note: A stroke through a number selects the second syllable table (DECODE marks it '+'); struck N, R, g, 4 are nulls.

system.notes: distinct_symbols counted with parse.py over DECODE's DOC_R*.txt (git-ignored). Struck 14 is not fixed (possibly 'ju'); tan (Flandes?) and cun iles (españoles?) are conjectural. 116 = V.S.; 8 is used for o.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments in the left margin of all ten letters (eight recognised by DECODE; faint ones on R1004/R1005 found during this work)

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE login (session cookie) for the transcriptions and images.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R1002-R1011 images and DECODE's DOC_*.txt ciphertext transcriptions with the stored cookie.
parse.py token counts over the ten transcriptions; n, r, s (20, 24, 25) the commonest tokens.
Lined the 4 Sept letter (R1010) up against its marginal decipherment; the key structure (letters 9-30, syllables 31-60, struck table, disguised letter pairs, code words) followed.
Applied the rebuilt key (dec.py) to all ten transcriptions, including R1004 and R1005 listed as non-decrypted.
Faint marginal decipherments on R1004 and R1005 found and compared; they agree with the key reading. The key reproduces the other eight margins.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3366 tokens, 192 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.259 per letter; random keys -4.152 (z 8.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.63 (mean -2.655, z 29.8); annealer on the real text -2.559. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): DECODE ciphertext transcriptions (DOC_*.txt, previously only in the git-ignored img/) copied to decode/; decryptions are the machine readings read/R*.raw.txt (dec.py), plus the normalised R1004/R1005 text copied from NOTES; key table copied from NOTES to texts/key.md. The contemporary margin decipherments of the eight are not transcribed.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.259; polyphony 0.0; 138 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.559

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The syllabic nomenclator was rebuilt by lining up the 4 Sept letter (R1010) with its contemporary marginal decipherment and then applied to all ten DECODE transcriptions; the reported text is the key's output, checked against the margins (the faint margins on R1004/R1005 were found after the key had read them).
outcome.fraction_read_source: read/R*.raw.txt, all ten letters: cipher tokens (3504); every {..} and [..] counted unread (136), including {8}=o and [e]=lle and DECODE's inserted margin words; nonsense syllables from DECODE slips not detectable and counted read
outcome.notes: Key rebuilt here from the letters with the marginal decipherments (complete, contemporary) in hand, so attack is archive decipherment rather than cryptanalysis. Open in the key: struck 14 and a few struck numbers ([55], [25], [80], ...); three code words conjectural. The eight margin letters are summarised from the machine reading, not edited line by line.

credits.note: marginal decipherments of all ten letters; the key rebuilt from R1010's

texts.label: R1010, Rome 4 Sept 1677
texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: The French fleet has left Messina; rumoured bound for Brindisi, its design is Catania. Carpio is dismayed by news from Brussels that the Prince of Orange raised the siege of Charleroi "intempestivamente".

texts.label: R1011, Rome 18 Sept 1677
texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: Rome's reaction to Charleroi: anti-Spanish rumours are stirring the populace, Carpio has had no satisfaction from the Pope or his ministers, the militia of the district was called out and guns were mounted on Castel Sant'Angelo.

texts.label: R1009, Rome 25 Sept 1677
texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: False rumours are spread against the Spaniards; Carpio pressed the Pope for remedy and got neither remedy nor an inquiry, and has referred the matter to the viceroy of Naples and the governor of Milan.

texts.label: R1006, Rome 2 Oct 1677
texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: The offences to the Spanish nation continue; he has asked the governor of Milan and the cardinals of the Spanish party for advice. The French fleet and galleys kept station off Catania and then returned to Toulon, much battered.

texts.label: R1007, Rome 9 Oct 1677
texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: Still no satisfaction; on the cardinals' advice he stays away from papal audiences, awaiting the viceroy of Naples' answer.

texts.label: R1008, Rome 16 Oct 1677
texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: No news at this court; he stands firm and awaits orders on how to proceed.

texts.label: R1004, Rome 13 Nov 1677
texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: Carpio laments Spain's ill fortune: the Cardinal d'Estrées's arrival at Turin threatens some novelty in Italy and Flanders is in the state Fuenmayor knows; the Congress must wait on the Prince of Orange's meeting with the King of England; the King's orders have not yet come. DECODE lists it as non-decrypted.

texts.label: R1005, Rome 20 Nov 1677
texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: The signs that the next campaign will bring war in Milan cause great concern, the Cardinal d'Estrées at Turin not being idle. DECODE lists it as non-decrypted.

texts.label: R1002, Rome 4 Dec 1677
texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: On the King's orders he asked Innocent XI for an audience on the pending disputes; the Pope refused it twice and would receive the King's business only through a cardinal, so Carpio declines to treat the principal business until the point is settled.

texts.label: R1003, Rome 11 Dec 1677
texts.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: The loss of Freiburg may force the imperial troops back over the Rhine; the miserable state of Flanders; the Pope refused audience again; he awaits the Marqués de los Vélez, viceroy of Naples.
